headline: 300,000+ fled fighting in western Yemen, almost all in the past two months
dek: [CATCH-UP, IN-WINDOW RELAY] More than 300,000 people have fled their homes in western Yemen because of intensifying fighting between the Ansar Allah and Saudi-backed government forces, almost all of them in the past two months, and they urgently need shelter, food, clean water and health care, per…
sources: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Sunday statement, via AFP and Arab News
fault_line: Humanitarian toll of the Yemen escalation vs the military campaign: does the 300,000 displacement figure change how the Dawn of Yemen offensive is judged?

sections.what_happened: [CATCH-UP, IN-WINDOW RELAY] More than 300,000 people have fled their homes in western Yemen because of intensifying fighting between the Ansar Allah and Saudi-backed government forces, almost all of them in the past two months, and they urgently need shelter, food, clean water and health care, per IOM. IOM Yemen chief of mission Abdusattor Esoev: families fleeing 'with little more than the clothes on their backs'. IOM says it needs $45 million over the next six months for emergency assistance. Detail figures from IOM via Arab News: 43,000+ fled Al-Madaribah Wa Al-Aarah (Lahj) since Oct 1 (highest of any district); Aden now hosts 56,000+ displaced; Taiz clashes cut access and drove up to fivefold price rises on essentials; IOM has five mobile medical teams across Taiz, Marib, Lahj and Aden but demand outpaces response. SCOPE NOTE: this IOM 300,000+ figure (western Yemen, past two months) is distinct from the OCHA figure of 290,000+ since August cited in Oct 30 UN briefings (see counterevidence) -- do not merge the two scopes. This item was missed by the 20:00 scan; the Arab News relay (20:08 ) falls inside this window.
sections.what_verified: AFP (T1) via Times of Israel liveblog and Dawn live blog; Arab News (T3) reporting the IOM statement directly; IOM (T3 per registry IOM DTM row; the statement itself is primary)
sections.what_disputed: OCHA's Oct 30 briefing figure is 290,000+ displaced since August (different window/scope, not a contradiction); UNHCR separately warns 65,000+ refugees/asylum seekers in Yemen face worsening conditions. No Ansar Allah-side displacement figure located; the IOM figure covers western Yemen only, not national displacement (5.2m pre-existing IDPs per OCHA Oct 30 briefing).
sections.why_matters: 300,000 fled western Yemen in two months -- the war's human ledger while the strikes continue: IOM's number, the $45m ask, and the Taiz price spike.
sections.context: Background: Yemen displacement -- IOM: 300,000+ fled fighting in western Yemen, almost all in the past two months (Sunday statement; Arab News relay in-window 20:08 )

totw_analysis: Our read: 300,000 fled western Yemen in two months -- the war's human ledger while the strikes continue: IOM's number, the $45m ask, and the Taiz price spike. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Humanitarian toll of the Yemen escalation vs the military campaign: does the 300,000 displacement figure change how the Dawn of Yemen offensive is judged?
